title: Node identity, endpoint observations and device admission
summary: Storage Fabric keeps stable node identity separate from provider, routable endpoint, observed block devices and admitted workspace capacity. A visible disk is not allocatable until explicitly admitted, and Storage fleet assessment emits per-node storage evidence without taking Job-to-Node placement authority.
invariants: nodeId is the stable join key; provider and IP/endpoint are attributes/observations, not identity.
A block device discovered by fdisk or equivalent is evidence of presence, not workspace admission.
UNQUALIFIED devices create no StoragePool and contribute no allocatable bytes.
Unknown capacity is not invented; a node with no admitted pool/capacity observation is storage-INFEASIBLE.
Separate nodes and separate capacity domains are never summed into one ordinary workspace.
StorageFleetPlacementAdvisor returns a matrix of storage evidence and does not select the final placement winner.
Endpoint reachability is not authenticated liveness; Job-to-Node retains liveness, hard eligibility, ranking and lease authority.
Disposable service lifecycle still dominates physical media quality: Azure trial capacity is working space, not durable safety.

provenance.claim: Regression proves stable node/provider/endpoint separation, device-admission persistence and disposable Azure lifecycle.
Regression proves four-node ED209 storage matrix, no invented AWS capacity, no aggregation of Oracle nodes, and no use of unqualified Azure devices.
